unit: Ch 2: Incorporation of Company and Matters Incidental Thereto
note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Introduction to Incorporation & Promoter
explain: A promoter initiates the formation of a company and brings it into legal existence.
Promoters are named in a prospectus or annual return, or control affairs, or direct the Board.
Persons acting purely in a professional capacity (like legal advisors or CAs) are not promoters.
Promoters stand in a fiduciary position towards the company they form.

flow.title: Promoter Identification Process
steps: Conceive business idea & project plan
Take steps to form the company
Name in prospectus or annual return
Exercise control over company affairs
Act in fiduciary role for incorporation

topics.example: An entrepreneur who conceives a tech startup concept, hires lawyers, drafts initial plans, and registers the firm is a promoter.
remember: Professional advisors acting in professional capacity are NOT promoters.
Promoters remain liable for fraud or misstatement in incorporation documents.
mistakes: Assuming a CA or lawyer helping with registration is automatically a promoter.
Thinking a promoter must be associated with the company only at initial formation and cannot join later.

quiz.q: Which of the following persons is considered a promoter under Section 2(69)?
o: A solicitor giving legal advice on incorporation
A person named as promoter in the annual return
A chartered accountant filing incorporation forms for a fee
A banker providing standard banking services
quiz.why: Section 2(69) explicitly includes individuals identified as promoters in the annual return, excluding mere professional advisors.

quiz.q: Are professional advisors who guide incorporation treated as promoters?
o: No, if acting purely in a professional capacity
Yes, if they charge a fee
quiz.why: The definition under Section 2(69) specifically excludes persons acting merely in a professional capacity.

topics.title: Formation of Company
explain: A company can be formed for any lawful purpose by subscribing names to the Memorandum.
Minimum membership required: Public company (7 persons), Private company (2 persons), OPC (1 person).
Companies may be limited by shares, limited by guarantee, or have unlimited liability.

flow.title: Steps in Forming a Company
steps: Determine company type and liability structure
Gather minimum required subscribers
Subscribe names to the Memorandum
Comply with statutory registration requirements

topics.example: Seven individuals coming together to subscribe to a memorandum and register a public limited manufacturing business.
remember: Public company min members = 7.
Private company min members = 2.
One Person Company min members = 1.
mistakes: Thinking a private company can be formed by a single person without meeting OPC requirements.
Confusing guarantee companies with companies limited by shares.

quiz.q: What is the minimum number of subscribers required to form a public company?
quiz.why: Section 3(1)(a) requires seven or more persons to form a public company.

quiz.q: Under Section 3, how many members are needed to form a standard private company (other than OPC)?
quiz.why: Section 3(1)(b) states a private company may be formed by two or more persons.

topics.title: One Person Company (OPC)
explain: An OPC is a private company with only one natural person as a member.
The member must be an Indian citizen, whether resident in India or otherwise.
Resident in India means staying in India for at least 120 days in the preceding financial year.
The MOA must name a nominee who becomes member on the sole member's death or incapacity.
OPC cannot convert to or be formed as a Section 8 (charitable) company or conduct NBFC activities.

flow.title: OPC Nominee Appointment & Change Flow
steps: Select natural person as nominee
Obtain nominee's prior written consent
Specify nominee name in MOA
Submit written consent to ROC
File change within 30 days if nominee replaced

topics.example: Ms. Madhu forms an OPC and names Mr. Sudan as nominee; if Ms. Madhu becomes incompetent, Mr. Sudan becomes the sole member.
remember: A person can be a member of only 1 OPC and nominee of only 1 OPC at a time.
If dual membership occurs by nomination, it must be resolved within 180 days.
Nominee change requires filing notice with ROC within 30 days.
mistakes: Believing a minor or corporate body can incorporate an OPC.
Assuming changing a nominee alters the Memorandum of Association.

quiz.q: What is the minimum stay in India required in the preceding FY for a person to be considered a 'Resident in India' for OPC?
quiz.why: As per Rule 3 of Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014, resident in India means staying for not less than 120 days during the preceding financial year.

quiz.q: Within how many days must a company notify the ROC regarding a change in nominee of an OPC?
quiz.why: The company must file notice of nominee change with the Registrar within 30 days of receipt of intimation.

topics.title: Members Severally Liable in Certain Cases (Reduction of Membership)
explain: Applies when membership falls below 7 (public) or 2 (private) and business carries on beyond 6 months.
Every remaining member cognizant (aware) of this fact becomes personally liable for debts.
Personal liability applies to debts contracted after the 6-month period elapsed.
Lenders can sue such cognizant members individually (severally) for those post-6-month debts.

flow.title: Triggering of Personal Liability under Section 3A
steps: Membership drops below minimum threshold
Company continues business for > 6 months
Remaining members are aware of shortfall
Personal several liability applies to post-6-month debts

topics.example: A public company drops to 5 members and operates for 8 months; remaining 5 aware members are personally liable for debts taken in months 7 and 8.
remember: Liability attaches ONLY AFTER 6 months of operating below statutory minimum.
Only members aware of the reduced membership are personally liable.
mistakes: Thinking members are liable for debts contracted during the first 6 months of reduction.
Believing unaware members are also automatically held personally liable.

quiz.q: Under Section 3A, personal liability of remaining members begins after the company carries on business below minimum membership for more than:
quiz.why: Section 3A specifies that personal liability applies if business is carried on for more than six months with reduced members.

quiz.q: For which debts are cognizant members personally liable under Section 3A?
o: Debts contracted during the first 6 months of reduction
Debts contracted after the elapse of 6 months
quiz.why: Members are severally liable for the payment of whole debts of the company contracted after the elapse of six months.

topics.title: Incorporation Procedure & Documents
explain: Registration application is filed with ROC in web form SPICe+ (INC-32).
Documents required: MOA (INC-33), AOA (INC-34), professional declaration (INC-8), subscriber declaration (INC-9).
INC-9 confirms subscribers/directors are not convicted of formation offenses or fraud in past 5 years.
ROC issues Certificate of Incorporation (INC-11) containing CIN and PAN.
Furnishing false information during incorporation attracts fraud liability u/s 447 and NCLT action.

flow.title: Incorporation Process Flow
steps: Draft MOA (INC-33) and AOA (INC-34)
Obtain declarations (INC-8 & INC-9)
Submit web form SPICe+ with fees
ROC verifies and registers documents
ROC issues Certificate of Incorporation (INC-11) with CIN

topics.example: Filing SPICe+ online with attached digital signatures and declarations to obtain an e-Certificate of Incorporation for a new software firm.
remember: Form INC-8 = Professional compliance declaration.
Form INC-9 = Subscriber & first director declaration.
Form INC-11 = Certificate of Incorporation containing 21-digit CIN.
mistakes: Believing the Certificate of Incorporation is conclusive proof that all prior acts were legal (NCLT can wind up illegal object companies).
Forgetting that false registration details invite fraud action under Section 447.

quiz.q: Which form is used for the professional declaration of compliance during incorporation?
quiz.why: Declaration of compliance by an advocate/CA/CS in practice is filed in Form No. INC-8.

quiz.q: What powers does NCLT have if a company was incorporated by suppressing material facts?
o: Direct that member liability shall be unlimited
Order removal of company name from register
quiz.why: Section 7(7) empowers NCLT to regulate management, make liability unlimited, remove name, or order winding up.

topics.title: Formation of Companies with Charitable Objects
explain: Section 8 companies promote commerce, art, science, sports, education, research, charity, environment, etc.
Profits must be applied solely to promote its objects; dividend payment to members is strictly prohibited.
Registered with limited liability without adding 'Limited' or 'Private Limited' to its name.
Central Government (delegated to ROC/RD) grants license and can revoke it on contravention.
On license revocation, CG can order winding up or amalgamation with another Section 8 company having similar objects.

flow.title: Section 8 License & Registration Flow
steps: Draft MOA with charitable/social objects
Apply in SPICe+ for Section 8 License
Obtain license from ROC
Register company without 'Limited' suffix
Apply all profits to objects and omit dividend

topics.example: A non-profit foundation formed to build free primary schools, using all generated surplus to open more schools.
remember: OPC and Small Company CANNOT be formed as or converted into Section 8 companies.
General meeting notice period for Section 8 company is 14 clear days (instead of 21 days).
mistakes: Assuming a Section 8 company can distribute profits as dividends to its members.
Thinking a Section 8 company needs 'Limited' at the end of its name.

quiz.q: Which of the following is STRICTLY prohibited for a Section 8 company?
o: Payment of dividend to its members
quiz.why: Section 8(1)(c) mandates that the company must intend to prohibit payment of any dividend to its members.

quiz.q: What is the penalty range for a Section 8 company that defaults in complying with section requirements?
quiz.why: Under Section 8(11), defaulting company is punishable with fine from ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore.

topics.title: Effect of Registration
explain: From the date specified in the Certificate of Incorporation, subscribers become a body corporate.
The company gains an independent corporate legal identity separate from its members.
Acquires perpetual succession, surviving changes or deaths in membership.
Gains legal capacity to acquire, hold, and dispose of property (movable/immovable, tangible/intangible).
Obtains power to contract, sue, and be sued in its own name.

flow.title: Legal Status Transition upon Registration
steps: Subscribers submit registration application
ROC issues Certificate of Incorporation
Company becomes a distinct body corporate
Acquires perpetual succession & property holding rights
Obtains right to contract and sue in its own name

topics.example: A company buying commercial office space in its corporate name rather than in the names of individual shareholders.
remember: Perpetual succession means company existence is unaffected by death, insolvency, or insanity of members.
Company property belongs to the company, not to its shareholders.
mistakes: Thinking shareholders directly own the assets of the company.
Assuming a company dies when all its original shareholders pass away.

quiz.q: From what date does a company become a body corporate with perpetual succession?
o: From date specified in Certificate of Incorporation
quiz.why: Section 9 states that body corporate status begins from the date of incorporation specified in the Certificate.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT a consequence of registration under Section 9?
o: Power to hold property in its own name
Personal liability of shareholders for normal debts
Capacity to sue and be sued
quiz.why: Registration creates a separate legal entity with limited liability; shareholders are not personally liable for normal corporate debts.

topics.title: Memorandum of Association (MOA) & Doctrine of Ultra Vires
explain: MOA is the fundamental charter of the company defining its powers and scope of activities.
Mandatory clauses: Name, Situation (State), Objects, Liability, Capital, Subscription, Nomination (OPC).
Doctrine of Ultra Vires: Any act beyond the objects clause of MOA is ultra vires and completely void.
An ultra vires act CANNOT be ratified even by 100% unanimous assent of shareholders.
Case reference: Ashbury Railway Carriage and Iron Co. Ltd. v. Riche.

flow.title: Doctrine of Ultra Vires Execution Test
steps: Check proposed action against MOA Objects clause
If inside objects: Act is valid and binding
If outside objects: Act is ultra vires
Ultra vires act is void ab initio
Shareholders cannot ratify ultra vires act

topics.example: A company with MOA objects limited to sugar manufacturing enters a contract to build real estate; contract is ultra vires and void.
remember: Acts ultra vires the Directors/Articles can be ratified by shareholders.
Acts ultra vires the Memorandum can NEVER be ratified.
mistakes: Confusing acts ultra vires the Articles (ratifiable) with acts ultra vires the Memorandum (non-ratifiable).
Thinking an ultra vires contract becomes valid if all shareholders vote to approve it later.

quiz.q: What is the legal status of an act performed by a company that goes beyond its MOA objects clause?
o: Valid if ratified by majority shareholders
Ultra vires and null & void ab initio
quiz.why: Under the Doctrine of Ultra Vires, any act beyond MOA powers is completely ultra vires and void, incapable of ratification.

quiz.q: Which landmark judicial case established the Doctrine of Ultra Vires in corporate law?
o: Ashbury Railway Carriage and Iron Co. Ltd. v. Riche
Daimler Co. Ltd. v. Continental Tyre Co.
quiz.why: Ashbury Railway Carriage & Iron Co. Ltd. v. Riche (1875) is the classic House of Lords ruling establishing ultra vires doctrine.

topics.title: Articles of Association (AOA) & Entrenchment Provisions
explain: AOA contains internal regulations and rules for managing the company's internal affairs.
Model forms of AOA are provided in Tables F, G, H, I, J of Schedule I.
Entrenchment provisions make alteration of specific clauses harder than passing a special resolution.
Entrenchment can be introduced at formation or later (agreed by all members in private co / special resolution in public co).
Notice of entrenchment must be filed with ROC in form SPICe+ (incorporation) or MGT-14 (within 30 days).

flow.title: Adding Entrenchment to AOA
steps: Identify clause needing stronger protection
At formation: Insert entrenchment in draft AOA
Post formation (Private): Obtain assent of ALL members
Post formation (Public): Pass Special Resolution
File Notice with ROC in MGT-14 within 30 days

topics.example: A private company inserting a clause that share forfeiture rules can only be altered with 95% majority instead of standard 75%.
remember: Private company entrenchment post-formation requires unanimous consent of ALL members.
Public company entrenchment post-formation requires a Special Resolution.
mistakes: Believing a public company needs 100% member consent to insert entrenchment provisions.
Forgetting to notify ROC about entrenchment provisions.

quiz.q: How can entrenchment provisions be added to the AOA of an existing PRIVATE company?
quiz.why: Section 5(4) requires agreement by all members of the company in the case of a private company.

quiz.q: Within how many days must an existing company file Form MGT-14 with ROC after entrenching its articles?
quiz.why: Rule 10 of Companies (Incorporation) Rules requires filing notice in Form MGT-14 within 30 days of entrenchment.

topics.title: Doctrine of Constructive Notice & Doctrine of Indoor Management
explain: Constructive Notice: MOA & AOA are public documents (u/s 399); outsiders dealing with company are presumed to know their contents.
Indoor Management (Turquand's Rule): Outsiders dealing with company can presume internal regularities/approvals have been satisfied.
Case reference for Indoor Management: Royal British Bank v. Turquand.
Exceptions to Indoor Management: Knowledge of irregularity, negligence/suspicion, forgery, lack of authority/agency.

flow.title: Applying Indoor Management vs Constructive Notice
steps: Outsider contracts with company
Outsider presumed to know public MOA/AOA (Constructive Notice)
Outsider assumes internal approvals done (Indoor Management)
Check for exceptions: Forgery, Negligence, Actual Knowledge
If exception present: Protection lost; contract invalid

topics.example: If directors borrow funds without general meeting resolution required by AOA, innocent lender is protected under Indoor Management.
remember: Doctrine of Indoor Management protects OUTSIDERS against internal irregularities.
Doctrine of Constructive Notice protects the COMPANY against outsiders.
Forgery is a total exception; Indoor Management NEVER validates forged documents.
mistakes: Applying Indoor Management when the outsider had actual knowledge of internal irregularity.
Thinking Indoor Management can protect a party relying on a forged stock certificate.

quiz.q: The Doctrine of Indoor Management provides protection to:
quiz.why: The Turquand's rule protects outsiders dealing in good faith from internal procedural irregularities.

quiz.q: Which of the following is an EXCEPTION where Doctrine of Indoor Management does NOT protect the outsider?
quiz.why: Forgery is a complete exception; a company can never be bound by forged documents under indoor management.

topics.title: Act to Override MOA/AOA & Effect of MOA/AOA
explain: Section 6: The Companies Act overrides any conflicting provision in MOA, AOA, agreements, or Board/GM resolutions.
Any provision in MOA/AOA inconsistent with the Act is void to the extent of inconsistency.
Section 10: Registered MOA and AOA constitute a binding legal contract between company and members, and members inter se.
MOA/AOA do NOT constitute a contract between the company and third-party outsiders.

flow.title: Section 6 Overriding Mechanism
steps: Identify clause in MOA / AOA / Resolution
Compare with provisions of Companies Act
Check for saving clause (e.g., 'Save as otherwise provided')
If direct conflict exists: Act overrides; clause is void

topics.example: An AOA clause allowing dividend payment out of capital is void because Section 123 of the Act requires dividends to be paid from profits.
remember: Company to Member: Company bound to observe articles.
Member to Company: Member bound to pay dues/calls.
Member to Member: Members bound inter se.
Outsider to Company: NO contract created by AOA.
mistakes: Believing an outsider can enforce a clause in AOA granting them rights (e.g., Browne v. La Trinidad).
Thinking an agreement approved by all directors can override statutory provisions of the Act.

quiz.q: Under Section 6, if an AOA clause conflicts with a provision of the Companies Act 2013, the clause is:
o: Void to the extent of conflict
quiz.why: Section 6 states that provisions of the Act override conflicting terms in MOA/AOA, making inconsistent terms void.

quiz.q: Can a third-party outsider enforce a right granted to him solely under the company's AOA?
o: No, AOA does not create a contract with third-party outsiders
quiz.why: Section 10 creates contractual binding between company and members, but not between company and third-party outsiders.

topics.title: Alteration of Memorandum of Association & Rectification of Name
explain: MOA alteration requires a Special Resolution passed by members.
Name change requires Central Government (ROC) approval; impossible if company defaulted on filings or deposit repayments.
Section 16: CG (RD) can direct name rectification if name is identical/resembling existing company or registered trademark.
Trademark owner must apply within 3 years of incorporation/name change.
Company must rectify name within 3 months of direction by passing an Ordinary Resolution.

flow.title: Section 16 Rectification of Name Procedure
steps: CG/RD forms opinion or receives Trademark application
Application by TM owner filed within 3 years
CG issues direction to change name
Company passes Ordinary Resolution within 3 months
File Notice with ROC within 15 days; ROC issues fresh COI

topics.example: A company registered as 'Taxmann Advisory Pvt Ltd' rectified its name within 3 months via ordinary resolution upon CG direction under Section 16.
remember: Name rectification u/s 16 requires ORDINARY Resolution within 3 MONTHS.
Voluntary name change u/s 13 requires SPECIAL Resolution and CG/ROC approval.
Trademark owner application limit = 3 years from registration.
mistakes: Confusing 3 months time limit for Section 16 rectification with standard Section 13 alteration rules.
Thinking Section 16 name rectification requires a Special Resolution instead of an Ordinary Resolution.

quiz.q: Within what period must a trademark owner file an application to CG for name rectification under Section 16?
quiz.why: Section 16(1)(b) specifies that trademark proprietor must apply within three years of incorporation or registration of change of name.

quiz.q: What type of resolution must a company pass to comply with CG direction for name rectification u/s 16?
quiz.why: Section 16 mandates changing name within 3 months after adopting an Ordinary Resolution.

topics.title: Alteration of Articles of Association & Updation of Copies
explain: AOA alteration requires passing a Special Resolution.
Conversion of public company to private company requires approval of Central Government (Regional Director).
Application to RD for public-to-private conversion must be filed within 60 days of special resolution in Form RD-1.
Altered articles and RD order must be filed with ROC within 15 days in Form INC-27.
Section 15: Every alteration must be noted in every copy of MOA/AOA issued; default penalty is ₹1,000 per copy.

flow.title: Public to Private Conversion via AOA Alteration
steps: Pass Special Resolution to alter AOA
Apply to RD in e-Form RD-1 within 60 days
Obtain RD approval order
File order and altered AOA in INC-27 with ROC within 15 days
Update all issued copies of MOA/AOA (u/s 15)

topics.example: A public company altering its AOA to insert private company restrictions, obtaining RD order, and updating all physical/electronic copies.
remember: Conversion of Public to Private Co requires RD Approval.
Conversion of Private to Public Co does NOT require RD approval.
Filing of altered AOA with ROC = 15 days (Form INC-27).
Penalty u/s 15 = ₹1,000 per copy issued without alteration.
mistakes: Forgetting to file altered AOA with ROC within 15 days.
Assuming conversion of private to public company needs Regional Director approval.

quiz.q: Within how many days must an application for converting a public company to private company be filed with RD after Special Resolution?
quiz.why: Rule 41 of Incorporation Rules requires application to RD in e-Form RD-1 within 60 days of passing special resolution.

quiz.q: What is the penalty under Section 15 for issuing copies of AOA without noting alterations?
quiz.why: Section 15(2) states that company and officer in default are liable to a penalty of ₹1,000 for every copy issued without alteration.

topics.title: Registered Office of Company
explain: Company must establish registered office within 30 days of incorporation (60 days for IFSC) and file verification (INC-22).
Name and registered office address must be painted/affixed outside all offices and printed on letters, notices, bills.
Shifting within same city: Board Resolution.
Shifting city within same ROC jurisdiction: Special Resolution.
Shifting between ROCs within same State: Special Resolution + RD Confirmation (INC-23).
Shifting from one State to another: Special Resolution + CG/RD Approval (INC-23).

flow.title: Registered Office Relocation Approvals
steps: Within same city: Board Resolution only
Outside city (same ROC): Special Resolution
One ROC to another (same State): SR + RD Confirmation
One State to another: SR + CG/RD Approval (INC-23)
File confirmation in INC-28 with ROCs within 30 days

topics.example: Shifting registered office from Mumbai (ROC Mumbai) to Pune (ROC Pune) requires a Special Resolution and RD approval.
remember: Verification of registered office filed within 30 days of incorporation.
Change notice to ROC for any address change = 30 days (INC-22).
Penalty for default u/s 12 = ₹1,000/day (max ₹1,00,000).
mistakes: Believing shifting registered office within the same city requires a Special Resolution (Board Resolution is sufficient).
Confusing state-to-state relocation with simple intra-city change.

quiz.q: What approval is required to shift a registered office from one city to another within the jurisdiction of the SAME Registrar?
quiz.why: Section 12(5) states that shifting outside local limits of city/town requires passing a Special Resolution.

quiz.q: Within how many days of incorporation must a standard company furnish verification of its registered office to ROC?
quiz.why: Section 12(2) mandates furnishing verification of registered office to Registrar within 30 days of incorporation.

topics.title: Commencement of Business
explain: Applies to companies incorporated after 2nd Nov 2018 having a share capital.
Cannot commence business or borrow funds unless two conditions are met:
1. Director files declaration in Form INC-20A within 180 days of incorporation stating subscribers paid agreed share value.
2. Verification of registered office filed with ROC under Section 12(2).
Failure to file INC-20A within 180 days gives ROC cause to initiate name removal (strike off).

flow.title: Commencement of Business Compliance Steps
steps: Incorporate company with share capital
Subscribers deposit money for agreed shares
File registered office verification (INC-22)
Director files declaration INC-20A within 180 days
Commence business operations and borrowing

topics.example: A newly incorporated tech company receiving initial share payment from founders and filing INC-20A before issuing bank loans.
remember: Time limit for filing INC-20A declaration = 180 days from incorporation.
Penalty: Company = ₹50,000; Officers in default = ₹1,000/day (max ₹1,00,000).
mistakes: Commencing business operations prior to filing Form INC-20A.
Confusing 180-day INC-20A deadline with 30-day registered office verification.

quiz.q: Within how many days from incorporation must Form INC-20A declaration be filed by a director?
quiz.why: Section 10A(1)(a) requires director declaration to be filed within 180 days from incorporation date.

quiz.q: What is the fixed penalty imposed on a company for failing to comply with Section 10A commencement provisions?
quiz.why: Section 10A(2) states that company in default shall be liable to a penalty of fifty thousand rupees.

topics.title: Conversion of Companies Already Registered
explain: Empowers a registered company of any class to convert into another class by altering MOA & AOA.
Company files an application with ROC with required documents.
ROC satisfies compliance, closes former registration, and issues fresh Certificate of Incorporation.
Conversion does NOT affect debts, liabilities, obligations, or contracts incurred prior to conversion.
Prior obligations remain enforceable as if conversion had not taken place.

flow.title: Conversion of Existing Company Flow
steps: Pass resolutions to alter MOA and AOA
Apply for conversion with ROC
ROC verifies statutory compliance
ROC closes former registration entry
ROC issues fresh Certificate of Incorporation

topics.example: Converting a private company into a public company; existing bank loan obligations remain fully binding on the converted public company.
remember: Conversion does NOT create a new legal entity; it alters status.
Pre-existing debts and liabilities remain fully valid post-conversion.
mistakes: Believing conversion discharges the company from pre-conversion liabilities.
Thinking a company needs to liquidate and re-incorporate to change class.

quiz.q: What happens to the existing liabilities of a company after it converts to another class under Section 18?
o: They remain fully enforceable against the company
quiz.why: Section 18(3) explicitly provides that conversion shall not affect any debts, liabilities, or contracts incurred prior to conversion.

quiz.q: Upon successful conversion under Section 18, the Registrar shall:
o: Close former registration and issue fresh Certificate of Incorporation
quiz.why: Section 18(2) specifies that ROC shall close former registration and issue a fresh Certificate of Incorporation.

topics.title: Subsidiary Company Not to Hold Shares in Holding Company
explain: A subsidiary company cannot hold shares in its holding company, and holding co cannot allot/transfer shares to subsidiary (void).
Extends to nominees of the subsidiary company.
EXCEPTIONS where subsidiary CAN hold shares in holding company:
a) Subsidiary holds shares as legal representative of a deceased member.
b) Subsidiary holds shares as a trustee.
c) Subsidiary was shareholder before becoming a subsidiary (cannot vote in GM).

flow.title: Section 19 Shareholding Prohibition & Exceptions
steps: Check general rule: Allotment/Transfer to subsidiary is VOID
Check Exception 1: Holding as legal representative
Check Exception 2: Holding as trustee
Check Exception 3: Shareholder before becoming subsidiary
If Exception 3 applies: Allow holding, but SUSPEND voting rights

topics.example: Company S holds 2% shares in Company H as a trustee for a trust; this holding is valid under Section 19 exception.
remember: General rule: Subsidiary holding shares in holding company = VOID.
Pre-existing shareholding exception = Allowed to hold, but NO voting right.
mistakes: Assuming a subsidiary can vote in general meetings of holding company for pre-existing shares.
Believing holding shares as a trustee is prohibited.

quiz.q: Under Section 19, can a subsidiary company exercise voting rights on shares held in its holding company prior to becoming a subsidiary?
quiz.why: Note (a) to Section 19 states that voting rights apply only for legal representative or trustee holdings, excluding pre-existing shareholding.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a VALID exception allowing a subsidiary to hold shares in its holding company?
o: As a legal representative of a deceased member
To help holding co meet minimum capital
quiz.why: Section 19(1) proviso explicitly permits holding shares as a legal representative of a deceased member.

topics.title: Service of Documents, Authentication & Execution of Bills/Deeds
explain: Sec 20: Documents served on company/officers by registered post, speed post, courier, leaving at office, or electronic mode.
Service of meeting notice by post is deemed effected 48 hours after posting.
Sec 21: Documents/contracts authenticated by any KMP or authorized officer/employee.
Sec 22: Bills of exchange/cheques executed by person acting under express/implied authority.
Deeds executed by attorney authorized under Common Seal OR signed by 2 directors (or 1 director + CS).

flow.title: Execution of Deeds under Section 22
steps: Check if company has Common Seal
If Yes: Authorize attorney in writing under Common Seal
If No: Authorize attorney signed by 2 Directors OR 1 Director + CS
Attorney executes deed on behalf of company
Deed binds company legally

topics.example: Two directors signing an authority letter empowering a project manager to execute land purchase contracts on behalf of the company.
remember: Notice of meeting sent by post = Deemed served at 48 hours after posting.
Execution of deeds without Common Seal requires signatures of 2 Directors OR 1 Director + Company Secretary.
mistakes: Believing a single director acting without authorization can execute a binding deed on behalf of a company without common seal.
Assuming postal delivery of meeting notice is deemed served immediately upon posting.

quiz.q: When is service of a notice of meeting deemed to be effected if sent by post under Section 20?
quiz.why: Section 20(2) specifies that notice of a meeting sent by post is deemed served at the expiration of 48 hours after posting.

quiz.q: In a company without a Common Seal, who must sign the authorization letter to execute deeds under Section 22?
o: 2 directors OR 1 director and Company Secretary
quiz.why: Section 22(2) states that without a common seal, authorization must be signed by 2 directors or by 1 director and the Company Secretary.
